subject: Transient headroom crediting & burst pricing structure
body:
From: Oliver Hayes <procurement@acme.ai>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 25 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated pool + burst credits question

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. Our engineering team ran the Q1 traffic dump against the recommended pool sizing and attached a trimmed usage CSV (Q1-usage-report.csv). We have two open items before procurement can sign:

1) Burst granularity — we deploy short, sharp spikes (1-6 minutes). Is Redwood able to meter burst usage in sub-10-minute granularity (credits per-minute or per-30s), or is it strictly slab-based (e.g., 1-hour buckets)?

2) Cooldown exceptions — during business-critical launches we need a temporary exception to cooldown rules (we may hit sustained elevated traffic for 45 minutes). Can a one-off manual override be included in the contract/SLAs?

We'd appreciate an addendum or simple language that outlines how short transient headroom is credited and how exceptions are handled.

Oliver
Procurement, Acme AI

-----

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Oliver Hayes <procurement@acme.ai>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 25 Mar 2027 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated pool + burst credits question

Hi Oliver — great to hear the report arrived. Short answers up front: we support both models in practice, and we can put contract language around an exception workflow. A few details below and a suggested addendum attached.

- Granularity: our Dedicated burst overlay can be configured either as slab-based (per-hour windows with slab pricing) or as a time-proportional credit model (per-minute billing for consumed headroom). The per-minute model reduces wasted credits for your short spikes but increases meter resolution and billing churn.

- Cooldown exceptions: we offer a documented exception process (request → approve → manual override) for one-off launches. We can add a clause that allows up to N exceptions per 12 months with 24-hour notice for planned launches, and an expedited option for emergency launches (subject to manual approval).

Attached is a draft_pricing_addendum.pdf with two options:
Option A: Per-minute headroom credits (recommended for Acme given the 1-6 minute spikes)
  - Baseline reserved commit: 200k vTokens/month (maps to ~12 GPUs sustained)
  - Per-minute headroom rate: $0.22 / vToken-minute (billed down to 30s increments)
  - Monthly committed discount: 15% off published Dedicated list for baseline usage
  - Up to 3 cooldown exceptions per year at no additional fee; expedited approvals possible at our discretion

Option B: Hourly slabs (simpler, slightly cheaper for sustained surges)
  - Baseline reserved commit: 220k vTokens/month
  - Hourly slab top-up: $500 per slab (1 hour slab = burst headroom for pool size X)
  - Monthly committed discount: 22% off listed Dedicated price for baseline usage
  - Exceptions handled case-by-case; standard approval SLA 48 hours

Next steps: if per-minute looks sensible we can run a modeled bill-for-month using your CSV and show expected spend vs option B. Marcus can own the bill model.

Best,
Kimberly Park\Account Executive, Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0198

-----Original Message-----
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 26 Mar 2027 08:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Dedicated pool + burst credits question

Kim, looping Marcus — I think per-minute billing is the right call for Acme. A few internal constraints to note before we surface Option A formally:

- Metering accuracy: per-minute requires finer telemetry and increases chargebacks; our billing backend supports 30s windows but not sub-second.
- Minimum price floor: per-minute has a minimum effective floor per minute to avoid microbilling overheads — we should show that in the example model.
- SLA: If we promise expedited manual overrides, we need a guardrail (e.g., max concurrency on overrides or a limit to avoid operational risk).

Marcus — can you run a model for both Option A and Option B against the attached CSV and include a sensitivity table for 2x and 4x burst amplitude? If we present that to Acme it will make the decision much easier.

Rishi
Head of Dedicated Sales, Redwood Inference

-----

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 26 Mar 2027 11:44:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated pool + burst credits question

Thanks Rishi — I ran three quick scenarios against the Q1 CSV. Summary (attached: modeled_bills.csv). Key takeaways:

- For short spikes (median 3 minutes) per-minute model dropped apparent cost by ~23% vs hourly slabs in our simulation because Acme has many microbursts that waste slab hours.
- If bursts sustain >20 minutes frequently, hourly slabs become cheaper. We should include a threshold clause: if average burst length >12 minutes over a rolling 30-day window we recommend rebaseline to a larger commit or switch to slab pricing.
- Operationally, addendum should include an "exception tokens" pool: we propose 10,000 emergency credits/year that can be applied immediately with an audit log entry; additional emergency credits bill at 1.5x standard headroom rate.

I suggest we propose Option A with the threshold fallback and the emergency pool. I'll attach a modeled_bills.csv and a one-page pricing bullets doc for the call.

— Marcus
Senior Pricing Analyst, Redwood Inference

-----

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Oliver Hayes <procurement@acme.ai>, Sanjay Rao <sanjay@acme.ai>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 28 Mar 2027 09:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Transient headroom crediting & burst pricing structure

Oliver / Sanjay — attaching the draft_pricing_addendum.pdf that reflects Marcus' model and Rishi's guardrails. Highlights of the proposed addendum:
- Primary: Per-minute headroom credits billed in 30s increments (recommended)
- Threshold clause: If average burst length >12 minutes over a 30-day rolling window, we trigger a commercial review and recommend moving to slab pricing or increasing the reserved commit.
- Exception workflow: 3 planned exceptions per 12 months free with 24-hour notice. Emergency exceptions: 10k emergency credits/year auto-apply; excess emergency credits billed at 1.5x per-minute rate.
- SLA for expedited manual override: target 4-hour response; subject to operator capacity limits described in appendix B.

Can we schedule a 30-min follow-up on Wednesday to walk the model? I can bring Rishi and Marcus and we can finalize language for procurement.

Best,
Kimberly

Thanks Kimberly — that looks actionable. Wednesday 11:00 PT works for Sanjay and me. We appreciate the emergency credit pool idea; that should cover our most volatile launches.

Please send over the calendar invite and the modeled_bills.csv beforehand so our finance team can review.

Oliver
Procurement, Acme AI
